A: Axial post-gadolinium MRI of the distal right femur showing an osteolytic, heterogeneously enhancing lesion involving diaphysis, metaphysis and epiphysis, with a black arrow annotation. The article is a case of a paediatric 'chondromyxoid fibroma-like' tumour (histologically an osteosarcoma mimic), so the attribution to chondromyxoid fibroma rests on the case being curated under this disease key; the epiphyseal/diaphyseal extent is atypical for chondromyxoid fibroma. Caption describes a black star while the visible marker is an arrow. B: Second post-gadolinium MR image of the same distal femoral lesion, showing a large enhancing intramedullary tumour with cortical remodelling and adjacent soft-tissue/muscle displacement. in_text_mentions: by radiography. The typical radiological features of a well-defined expansile radiolucent lesion with scalloped or lobulated margins, a sclerotic rim, septation, and no calcification were observed in all four cases of CMF (Figures 1 &2). Three patients with CMF of the foot and hand underwent curettage along with bone grafting using polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA). The patient with CMF of the anterior right second rib underwent a wide "enbloc" resection with chest wall reconstruction using Gore-Tex patch. None of the four patients had a recurrence after a mean duration of follow-up of 24 months.

in_text_mentions: The patient underwent endoscopic resection under general anesthesia. The mass was located below the middle turbinate and appeared well-circumscribed (Figure 3). After mucosal debridement, a firm, white mass was exposed, raising suspicion for a neoplastic process. Histopathological examination revealed multilobulated tissue with prominent myxoid stroma populated by uniform stellate and spindle cells and early chondroid matrix. (Figure 4). Immunohistochemical staining showed focal positivity for smooth muscle actin. These features were consistent with a diagnosis of chondromyxoid fibroma.

panels.rationale: Single-panel axial chest CT from a case of chondromyxoid fibroma of the right anterior second rib, with arrow indicating a radiolucent expansile rib lesion with cortical bubbling/blebbing; in-text states typical CMF radiological features including lobulated margins and sclerotic rim were seen in this case.
panels.attribution_text: Armah et al. Chondromyxoid fibroma of rib with a novel chromosomal translocation: a report of four additional cases at unusual sites.. Diagnostic pathology 2007. doi:10.1186/1746-1596-2-44. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Computed tomography scan of chest (case no. 2) demonstrating a radiolucent lesion of the right anterior second rib with cortical bubbling or blebbing, and without radiographic evidence of an acute fracture, calcification or malignancy (arrow). R indicates right side.
in_text_mentions: by radiography. The typical radiological features of a well-defined expansile radiolucent lesion with scalloped or lobulated margins, a sclerotic rim, septation, and no calcification were observed in all four cases of CMF (Figures 1 &2). Three patients with CMF of the foot and hand underwent curettage along with bone grafting using polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA). The patient with CMF of the anterior right second rib underwent a wide "enbloc" resection with chest wall reconstruction using Gore-Tex patch. None of the four patients had a recurrence after a mean duration of follow-up of 24 months.

panels.attribution_text: Vasudeva et al. Chondromyxoid Fibroma of Distal Phalanx of the Great Toe: A Rare Clinical Entity.. Cureus 2020. doi:10.7759/cureus.7133. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.

in_text_mentions: X-ray examination revealed a longitudinally oval lytic lesion in the right distal phalanx of great toe, involving almost the entire shaft, abutting the growth plate and eroding the medial cortex, “hemispheric bite like lesion as shown in Figure 2.” The margins were well defined, and there was no articular involvement. Computed tomography (CT) scan showed a well defined lytic lesion in the distal phalanx of great toe with internal septations, without any evidence of calcification or involvement of soft tissue (Figure 3). There was no periosteal reaction.

panels.rationale: Single-panel figure of an immunohistochemical (pan-cytokeratin) stain from the resected rib tumor of a human patient; the caption and in-text state the resection material confirmed a chondromyxoid fibroma. The visible hypocellular myxoid stroma with scattered spindle/stellate cells is consistent with the tumor, and the negative cytokeratin staining is the diagnostic point of the panel, but the immunophenotype is negative (absence of staining) and no positive, vocabulary-listed histologic feature is explicitly captioned, so confidence is moderate.
panels.attribution_text: Basak et al. Chondromyxoid Fibroma of the Rib: A Rare Benign Tumor With Potential for Local Recurrence.. Cureus 2021. doi:10.7759/cureus.19172. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 6.
panels.figure_caption: Immunohistochemical staining for pan-cytokeratin demonstrating negative staining of the tumor cells (10x magnification).
in_text_mentions: He underwent an en bloc resection of the left 12th rib and the surrounding muscle. A left posterior incision was made along the 12th rib. The rib was divided proximally to the tumor with a clear margin of about 1.5 cm. Histopathological examination of the resected material confirmed a chondromyxoid fibroma with clear surgical margins (Figures 4-6). On postoperative follow-up, he developed bulging of the abdominal wall of the left flank, but no true hernia. However, two years after surgery, he remains under CT surveillance with no signs of recurrence on CT scan.
